newsitem.title: USA: Biogen sues Amgen for patent infringement.
newsitem.headline: Biogen sues Amgen for patent infringement.

text.p: Biogen Inc filed suit late Wednesday against Amgen Inc, charging the California-based pharmaceutical with patent infringement concerning a drug used to treat Hepatitis C.

Biogen, in its suit filed in the U.S. District Court in Boston, alleges that Amgen's Infergen, a type of interferon that the Food and Drug Administration is expected to approve shortly, uses technology it developed for its interferon product, called Intro A.

The Cambridge, Mass.-based Biogen licensed Intro A, which is used in the treatment of various cancers as well as Hepatitis C, to Schering Corp, a unit of Schering-Plough Corp. Schering Corp filed a similar suit against Amgen last December in the U.S. District Court in Wilmington, Del.

Amgen spokesman David Kaye said his company's product Infergen is a "non-naturally occurring interferon" and the Thousand Oaks, Calif.-based concern is close to getting approval from the FDA for the drug in the treatment of Hepatitis C.

He estimated that some 250,000 Americans have been diagnosed with Hepatitis C, which he called "very common and widely under-diagnosed...It's thought that the number of sufferers could be well into the millions."
